source.title: PAC-Bayes Information Bottleneck
source.authors: Zifeng Wang; Shao-Lun Huang; E. Kuruoğlu; Ji-Meng Sun; Xi Chen; Yefeng Zheng

record.tranche_reason: Measures information stored in weights (IIW) as a different measure of generalization gap and reports width, batch-size, label-noise, and dropout results.
record.gate_note: Reported rows cover the paper's own experiments. Figure-based values are described as figure only where no exact numeric value is stated in the text. Results cited from other studies are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own training and test accuracy under width changes, label corruption, random-label training, and dropout. These bear on V1, V2, and V6. Its IIW measurements are a different construct, and its fixed-iteration batch experiment does not test V5's fixed-epoch claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors also emphasize fitting-to-compression transitions across activations and architectures. They conclude that IIW explains generalization behavior across width, label noise, and batch size, and that PIB achieves higher reported mean test accuracy than their baselines on all four datasets. The table does not establish statistically reliable superiority in every comparison.
record.recipe_differences: The study estimates information stored in weights using a Fisher-information-based measure and applies a PAC-Bayes information bottleneck; it does not reproduce the original studies' methods for the mapped claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with hidden-unit count, batch size, label corruption, dataset, and regularization method.

fits_no_version.finding: IIW decreases with width and tracks the generalization gap while weight norms increase.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Estimated information stored in weights tracks generalization gaps across network widths.

fits_no_version.finding: IIW increases with label corruption as test accuracy declines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Estimated information stored in weights tracks generalization gaps under label corruption.

fits_no_version.finding: Batch size 16 gives the best test accuracy and minimum IIW among the tested batches at equal iteration counts and learning rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch size affects held-out accuracy and IIW under fixed update budgets.

record.problems: Width and batch-size outcomes are shown in figures without exact values in the text. Batch-size comparison fixes iterations rather than epochs. The random-label experiment does not report a direct paired natural-label comparison. VGG comparison reports test accuracy but no training accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for the Figure 6 IIW trajectories or PIB test-accuracy comparisons were retained because these compare regularizers or the proposed PIB method rather than measuring the named dropout effect. Other reported values are not directly measures of the claim versions.

untested.parts: A fully documented paired natural-label versus fixed-random-label comparison using identical training recipes; the named convolutional architectures and ImageNet.
Downsampled CIFAR-10, confirmed training to convergence, and the original ReLU training protocol. An interpolation-threshold test-error peak is not required by V2 and is not established here.
All parts; no convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
All parts; no controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison.
All parts; batch sizes are compared at fixed iterations rather than fixed epochs, with no tests of the stated recipe adaptations.
Fully connected classifiers, systematic training-set-size and dropout-rate sweeps, excessive-dropout underfitting, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
All parts; IIW is not magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, and the required generalization-measure ranking comparison is absent.
All parts; no removal and retraining comparison based on memorization scores.

missing.what: Separate training-accuracy results across label-corruption levels, including the zero-corruption natural-label baseline. Section 5.3 explicitly says training accuracy changes little while test accuracy falls sharply; R5 records only test accuracy. These results are needed to assess the coexistence component of V1.

record.verdict_notes: No original-source exclusion applies. The absence of fixed-epoch experiments is an untested part of V5, not evidence limiting it. Figure 4's caption and the gap arithmetic contradict the prose's claim that declining training accuracy at constant test accuracy enlarges the gap.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare the same architecture and training recipe on fixed random versus natural labels with reported held-out accuracy for both.
Reports width effects on MNIST only; does not report downsampled CIFAR-10 or a test-error peak near the interpolation threshold.
Varies batch size with total iterations and learning rate held constant, not fixed epoch budgets; no language-model results or reported large-batch workload threshold.
Compares dropout in VGG-Net on four datasets; does not test fully connected classifiers, very small training sets, dropout rates, or joint removal of dropout and weight decay.

rows.subject: 2-layer MLP
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 with varying label corruption; training duration not stated
rows.operation_detail: Varied the label corruption ratio and measured train accuracy, test accuracy, and IIW.
rows.value: figure only; text states test accuracy decays sharply as noise increases
rows.locator: §5.3, Figure 4 left panel and accompanying text
rows.note: Training accuracy does not change much while test accuracy decays sharply as label noise increases; this is not a direct fixed-random-label versus natural-label comparison.
rows.check: The qualitative decline in test accuracy with corruption is relevant, but does not by itself establish V1's natural-label performance and nearly perfect random-label fit. Extract the natural-label baseline and corresponding training accuracy separately; do not interpret the decline itself as partial failure of V1.
